book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 2 · The Well-Being of the Paramedic
title: Staying Well and Safe: Stress, Grief, and Infection Control

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already wear PPE, lift with your legs, wash your hands and check scene safety. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Protect your body and mind: fitness, sleep, stress, burnout
  2. Support the dying and the grieving, then recover yourself
  3. Stay safe with needles, drugs and a crew to lead

Textbook: Chapter 2, PDF pages 105–178
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already know the safety basics: gloves and eye protection, lifting with your legs, washing your hands, and checking the scene before you go in. This chapter is about the person giving the care: you. As a PCP, the job asks more. You'll handle needles and drugs, you'll often lead the crew, and families will turn to you at the worst moments. Today: keeping your body and mind healthy over a long career, supporting the dying and the grieving and then recovering yourself, and the safety habits that matter more now that you're a PCP.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，安全基本功你们都会：戴手套和护目镜、用腿抬、洗手、进现场前先看安全。本章讲的是提供照护的那个人：你自己。当了 PCP，工作要求更高：你要处理针头和药物，常常要带领团队，家属也会在最糟糕的时刻向你求助。今天讲：怎样在漫长的职业生涯中保持身心健康；怎样陪伴临终者和悲痛的人，之后再让自己恢复；以及成为 PCP 后更加重要的安全习惯。

slides.title: Wellness: fuel, fitness, and sleep
slides.body:
• Plate: ½ vegetables and fruit, ¼ protein, ¼ whole grains
  • Water first; less caffeine; small snacks on shift
  • 30–60 min of moderate activity a day, in blocks of 10+ min
  • Target HR = (220 − age − resting HR) × 0.7 + resting HR
  • Shift work fights your circadian rhythm: keep a routine
  • Awake 18–20 hours? Rest before driving or giving drugs
slides.say: Wellness has physical, mental, and emotional parts. For food, Canada's Food Guide suggests a plate that's about half vegetables and fruit, a quarter protein, and a quarter whole grains, with water first. For fitness, aim for thirty to sixty minutes of moderate activity a day, even in ten-minute blocks. Target heart rate: two hundred twenty minus your age, minus your resting rate, times zero point seven, plus the resting rate. At age thirty with a resting rate of sixty, that's about one hundred fifty-one. And sleep: after eighteen to twenty hours awake, rest before you drive or give medications.
slides.sayZh: 健康包括身体、心理和情绪几个方面。饮食上，《加拿大食物指南》建议餐盘里大约一半蔬菜水果，四分之一蛋白质，四分之一全谷物，饮料首选水。运动上，每天三十到六十分钟中等强度活动，可以分成每段十分钟。目标心率：二百二十减年龄，再减静息心率，乘零点七，再加静息心率。三十岁、静息心率六十，大约是一百五十一。还有睡眠：连续清醒十八到二十小时后，先休息，才能开车或给药。

slides.title: Fight-or-flight: why hands shake
slides.body:
Big stressor→sympathetic surge→ready in under 20 seconds
  • Gains: pupils dilate, heart speeds up, airways open, glucose up
  • Costs: clumsy speech, poorer depth perception, jitters
  • Costs: fine motor control lost, just when you need it
  • On scene: slow breathing, then reframe ("I've practised this")
  • After the call: progressive muscle relaxation
slides.say: Under a big stressor, your sympathetic nervous system fires. In under twenty seconds your pupils dilate, your heart speeds up, your airways open, sugar is released, and blood moves from the gut to your muscles. The costs: clumsy speech, poorer depth perception, shaking, and loss of fine motor control. Think about what PCPs do with their hands: find a small vein, draw up an exact dose, read a tiny label. So learn your warning signs, like a pounding heart or shouting. On scene, slow your breathing and reframe your thoughts. After the call, try progressive relaxation: tense, then release, each muscle group.
slides.sayZh: 面对重大应激，交感神经系统启动。不到二十秒，你的瞳孔散大、心跳加快、气道扩张、血糖升高，血液从胃肠道转向肌肉。代价是：说话笨拙、深度感知变差、发抖、精细动作失控。想想 PCP 用双手做的事：找细小的静脉、抽取精确的剂量、看清很小的标签。所以要了解自己的预警信号，比如心跳狂跳、大声喊叫。在现场，放慢呼吸，重构你的想法。收队后，试试渐进式放松：依次绷紧、再放松各组肌肉。

slides.title: How patients react under stress
slides.body:
• Common feelings: fear, anxiety, depression, anger, confusion
  • Denial: "it's nothing" → get history from someone reliable
  • Regression: acting younger than their age
  • Projection: putting their own feelings onto others
  • Displacement: anger at the illness aimed at you
  • Different isn't wrong: ask before you touch
slides.say: Patients react with fear, anxiety, depression, anger, or confusion, and often with defence mechanisms, which are automatic and unconscious. Denial is playing down a serious problem, and since your history drives your treatment decisions, find a reliable family member or friend to fill the gaps. Regression is going back to younger behaviour; a frightened adult may become clingy and childlike. Projection is putting your own feelings or motives onto others. Displacement is aiming anger at a safer target: the patient is angry at the illness, and you're the closest person, so don't take it personally. And respect culture: ask permission before you touch.
slides.sayZh: 病人会出现恐惧、焦虑、抑郁、愤怒或意识混乱，还常常启动心理防御机制，这些是自动的、潜意识的。否认是淡化严重的问题；你的病史决定你的处置决定，所以要找可靠的家属或朋友补充。退行是退回更幼稚的行为，受惊的成年人可能变得黏人、像个孩子。投射是把自己的感受或动机安到别人身上。转移是把愤怒发向更安全的对象：病人其实在生疾病的气，而你离他最近，所以不要往心里去。还要尊重文化：触碰之前先征得同意。

slides.title: Families, bystanders, and big scenes
slides.body:
Families may panic or get angry, often from guilt. Your calm spreads.

Reaction at a multi-casualty sceneYour move
Anxiety: sweaty, shakyGive a specific task
Blind panic: no judgement, spreadsSeparate fast; a calm person watches
Depression: numb, dazedBring back to reality
Overreaction: chatter, rushingRemove from the treatment area
Conversion hysteria: sudden blindness or paralysisMove away from the scene
slides.say: Families are stressed too. They may panic, push you to hurry, or question your skills, and a parent's anger often comes from guilt. Stay calm and polite; your calm can settle the whole scene. At a multiple-casualty scene, the American Psychiatric Association describes five reactions. Anxiety, with sweating and shaking, passes in minutes; give a clear task. Blind panic is different: judgement disappears and it spreads, so separate that person fast and put them with someone calm. Depression looks numb and dazed. Overreaction is nonstop talking and rushing. Conversion hysteria turns anxiety into sudden blindness or paralysis.
slides.sayZh: 家属同样有压力：可能惊慌、催你快点、质疑你的能力，父母的愤怒往往来自内疚。保持冷静和礼貌，你的冷静能让整个现场平静下来。在多伤员现场，美国精神医学学会描述了五类反应。焦虑表现为出汗、发抖，几分钟就会过去，给他一个明确的任务。盲目恐慌不一样：判断力完全丧失，而且会传染，要尽快把他隔开，交给冷静的人看管。抑郁是麻木、发呆。过度反应是说个不停、四处乱跑。转换性癔症是把焦虑转成突然失明或瘫痪。

slides.q: At a multi-vehicle crash, a bystander is screaming and running between the cars, and other bystanders are starting to copy her. You're the PCP leading the scene. What's best?
options: Give her a simple task, like holding a dressing
Separate her quickly and put her with a calm person
Ignore her and focus only on the patients
Have her sit alone in the back of the ambulance
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. At a multi-vehicle crash, a bystander is screaming and running between the cars, and other bystanders are starting to copy her. You're the PCP leading the scene. What's best? A, give her a simple task, like holding a dressing. B, separate her quickly and put her with a calm person. C, ignore her and focus only on the patients. D, have her sit alone in the back of the ambulance. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。多车相撞现场，一名旁观者尖叫着在车辆之间乱跑，其他旁观者也开始跟着她跑。你是带领现场的 PCP。最好的做法是什么？A 给她一个简单任务，比如按住一块敷料；B 尽快把她隔开，交给一个冷静的人；C 不理她，只管病人；D 让她一个人坐到救护车后舱。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. This is blind panic: her judgement is gone and the panic is spreading, so she has to be separated quickly and watched by someone calm. A, a specific task, is the right move for anxiety, the sweaty, shaky reaction that passes in minutes, but not for panic. C lets the panic spread through the crowd. D leaves a person with no judgement alone and unsupervised.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。这是盲目恐慌：她的判断力已经丧失，恐慌还在扩散，所以要尽快把她隔开，交给冷静的人看管。A 给具体任务适用于焦虑，也就是出汗、发抖、几分钟就会过去的反应，不适用于恐慌。C 会让恐慌在人群中蔓延。D 让一个失去判断力的人独自待着、没人看管。

slides.title: Burnout: it's how you cope
slides.body:
Burnout depends on how you react to stress

  • False beliefs: "I must be perfect", "If they die, it's my fault"
  • Signs: fatigue, cynicism, dreading work, poor sleep
  • Also: lost hobbies, poor focus, frequent colds, alcohol or drugs
  • Prevent: sleep, good food, 30 min exercise 3–4 times a week
  • Friends outside EMS; talk it out; debrief after tough calls
slides.say: Burnout means your physical or emotional strength is used up, from chronic, unrelieved stress. But the textbook's key point is that burnout depends on how you react to stress, a reaction learned from what you believe. Watch for false beliefs like I must be perfect, or if a patient dies it's all my fault. As a PCP, with more weight on your decisions, they're easy to fall into. Learn the warning signs on the slide, in yourself and in your partner. Prevention: sleep, eat well, exercise at least thirty minutes three or four times a week, keep friends outside EMS, and debrief after tough calls.
slides.sayZh: 职业倦怠是指身体或情绪的力量被耗尽，来源是长期得不到缓解的压力。但书里的关键点是：倦怠取决于你怎样回应压力，而这种回应是从你的信念中习得的。留意错误信念，比如「我必须永远完美」「病人死了全是我的错」。作为 PCP，你的决定分量更重，更容易陷进去。记住幻灯片上的预警信号，留意自己，也留意搭档。预防：睡够、吃好、每周三到四次、每次至少三十分钟运动，保持急救圈外的朋友，艰难任务后做汇报讨论。

slides.title: Death and dying: five stages
slides.body:
Denial→Anger→Bargaining→Depression→Acceptance
  • Depression: don't cheer them up; let them grieve
  • Many dying patients want to talk: open the door, then listen
  • "Am I dying?" Be honest it's serious, but leave hope
  • Give control: explain, involve; write messages word for word
slides.say: Elisabeth Kübler-Ross described five stages of grief that dying people, and sometimes families, often move through: denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance. In anger, people ask why me, and it may land on you. In depression they go quiet; don't try to cheer them up, just let them be sad. In acceptance, the dying person lets go, and the family often needs you most. Many dying patients want to talk, so open the door gently and listen. If asked, am I going to die, be honest that it's serious without taking away all hope. And write any message they give you word for word.
slides.sayZh: 伊丽莎白·库伯勒-罗斯描述了临终者、有时还有家属常会经历的五个悲伤阶段：否认、愤怒、讨价还价、抑郁、接受。愤怒阶段，人会问「为什么是我」，怒气可能落到你身上。抑郁阶段，他们变得沉默：不要急着让他们振作，让他们难过就好。接受阶段，临终者开始放手，这时家属往往最需要你。很多临终病人想谈谈，所以要温和地打开话题，然后倾听。被问到「我会死吗」，要诚实承认情况严重，但不要夺走全部希望。他们托你带的话，要一字不差地写下来。

slides.title: When the family becomes your patient
slides.body:
• Let the family see the body; screen it from the public
  • Say "dead", not "passed away"
  • Don't rush to pack up the resuscitation gear
  • Give private time to say goodbye
  • Call a neighbour or clergy; accept guilt, shock and anger
  • Children 3–6 may think death is temporary: "It's not your fault"
slides.say: When a patient dies, the call isn't over: the family becomes your patient. Don't hide the body from the family, even if it's badly injured, but screen it from the public; people who never see the body can get stuck in denial. Say dead, not passed away. Don't rush to pack up the resuscitation gear; it shows everything was tried. Give them private time to say goodbye. Call a neighbour or their clergy, and accept whatever they feel. With children, age matters: three to six year olds may think death is temporary and blame themselves, so they need to hear it isn't their fault.
slides.sayZh: 病人去世了，任务并没有结束：家属成了你的病人。不要对家属隐藏遗体，哪怕伤得很重，但要对公众遮挡；没见到遗体的人容易卡在否认里。直接说「死了」，不说「走了」。不要急着收起复苏器材，它们说明一切都尝试过了。给家属单独告别的时间。请邻居或他们的神职人员来支持，并接受他们的任何情绪。孩子要看年龄：三到六岁的孩子可能以为死亡是暂时的，还会自责，所以他们需要听到「这不是你的错」。

slides.title: After a hard call
slides.body:
StepWhenWhat
DefusingRight after the callAbout 30 min; everyone involved talks
CISD24–72 hours laterAbout 3 hours; counsellors; confidential
PTSDWeeks to monthsFlashbacks, nightmares, withdrawal

No good evidence that CISD works: offer debriefing, never force it. PTSD signs? Tell your supervisor.
slides.say: Critical incidents overwhelm the people who run them: a colleague killed or badly hurt, a colleague's suicide, a multiple-casualty incident, or a child's serious injury or death. A defusing is a short session of about thirty minutes right after the call. A formal critical incident stress debriefing, or CISD, comes twenty-four to seventy-two hours later: about three hours, led by counsellors, confidential, away from work. But there's no good evidence it works, and it may even harm, so offer it, never force it. If weeks later you have flashbacks, nightmares, or pull away from people, that may be PTSD. Tell your supervisor.
slides.sayZh: 关键事件会压垮执行任务的人：同事殉职或重伤、同事自杀、多伤员事件，或者儿童重伤或死亡。缓解会是任务后立即进行、约三十分钟的简短会议。正式的关键事件压力汇报，也就是 CISD，在二十四到七十二小时后进行：约三小时，由咨询师主持，保密，离开工作场所。但没有可靠证据证明它有效，甚至可能有害，所以只能提供，绝不能强迫。如果几周后你出现闪回、噩梦，或开始疏远身边的人，可能是 PTSD，要告诉你的上级。

slides.title: Infection control with needles in hand
slides.body:
• Gloves every call; fresh pair after an IV start, before loading
  • Gloves off before you drive
  • Wash hands 30+ seconds with soap; alcohol wipes if no water
  • Possible TB: N95 respirator, not a surgical mask
  • Disinfect skin-contact gear; sterilize what enters the body
  • Every sharp straight into a sharps container
slides.say: As a PCP you also handle needles and blood, so details matter more. Gloves on every call, and after an IV start, consider a fresh pair before you load the patient. Gloves off before you drive. Wash with soap for at least thirty seconds; use alcohol wipes when there's no water. If tuberculosis is possible, wear an N95 respirator, not a surgical mask. Disinfection, for example with a one-to-ten bleach solution, kills many germs and is used on gear that touches skin. Sterilization kills all germs and is needed for anything that enters the body. And every needle goes straight into a sharps container.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你还要处理针头和血液，所以细节更重要。每次出车戴手套；开完静脉后，搬病人上车前考虑换一副新手套。开车前摘手套。用肥皂洗手至少三十秒；没有水时用酒精湿巾。可能有结核时，戴 N95 呼吸器，而不是外科口罩。消毒，比如用一比十的漂白水，能杀死大多数微生物，用于接触皮肤的器械；灭菌能杀死全部微生物，凡进入身体的东西都必须灭菌。每根针头都直接放进锐器盒。

slides.q: While you're starting an IV, the needle sticks your finger. The patient is stable and your partner takes over. What do you do first?
options: Finish the call, and report it later only if you feel sick
Wash the area right away with soap and water
Rub alcohol hand sanitizer on it and carry on
Wait for the patient's blood test before doing anything
slides.say: Here's a PCP safety question. While you're starting an IV, the needle sticks your finger. The patient is stable and your partner takes over. What do you do first? A, finish the call, and report it later only if you feel sick. B, wash the area right away with soap and water. C, rub alcohol hand sanitizer on it and carry on. D, wait for the patient's blood test before doing anything. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 安全题。你在开静脉时被针头扎到手指。病人情况稳定，搭档接手了。你第一步做什么？A 先完成任务，之后只有感到不舒服才上报；B 立即用肥皂和水清洗伤处；C 擦点酒精洗手液，继续工作；D 先等病人的血液检查结果再说。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. After any exposure to blood or body fluids, the first step is to wash the area immediately with soap and water. Then follow your local guidelines: report it as required, get a medical evaluation, get any immunization boosters you need, and document the incident and what you did to reduce the risk. A skips the required reporting and evaluation. C replaces the recommended soap-and-water wash. D delays steps that should start right away.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。接触血液或体液后，第一步是立即用肥皂和水清洗暴露部位。然后按本地规定：按要求上报、接受医学评估、补打需要的加强针，并记录事件经过和你为降低感染风险采取的措施。A 跳过了必须的上报和评估；C 用洗手液代替了推荐的肥皂水清洗；D 拖延了本该马上开始的步骤。

slides.title: Driving and dangerous scenes
slides.body:
• Lights and siren ask for the right of way; they don't demand it
  • Full stop at a red light; go once others see your intent
  • Running hot? Be able to justify it, and document why
  • Police first: fights, stabbings, shootings, domestics, vague calls
  • Hi-vis vest on before you step out at traffic scenes
  • Start sizing up a crash scene about 1.5 km out
slides.say: Your lights and siren ask for the right of way; they don't demand it. Stop fully at a red light, and go only when other drivers understand what you're doing. Before running lights and siren to hospital, ask whether the minutes saved will change the outcome, and be ready to justify and document it. When violence is known or expected, police go first: fights, stabbings, shootings, domestic disputes, and vague calls like person down. At traffic scenes, put on your high-visibility vest before you step out, and start sizing up the scene about a kilometre and a half away.
slides.sayZh: 警灯警笛是请求路权，不是要求路权。遇到红灯要完全停下，等其他司机明白你的意图后再走。开灯鸣笛送院前，问问自己：省下的几分钟能改变结果吗？要能说出理由并记录下来。已知或可以预见有暴力时，警察先进去：斗殴、刺伤、枪击、家庭纠纷，以及「有人倒地」这类含糊的呼叫。交通现场下车前先穿上高可见度背心，离现场大约一点五公里就开始观察。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Scene safety, PPE, routine precautions
  • Safe lifting; call for more hands early
  • Police first when violence is expected
  • Justify and document any lights-and-siren run
  • Calm, respectful care for upset people

PCP adds

  • Often the most trained on scene: sets the safety example
  • Handles sharps from IV starts; manages exposures
  • Protects fine-motor tasks from stress: breathe first
  • More drugs to give: none when exhausted
  • Gives a shaky partner a task; speaks up about burnout
slides.say: The left side is shared by every licence level: scene safety and PPE, safe lifting, calling for help, police first, justifying any lights-and-siren run, and calm, respectful care. On the right, the textbook notes that as a paramedic you'll often be the most trained person on scene, so the crew copies your safety habits. You handle sharps from IV starts, so you must manage exposures. Your most delicate tasks, like finding a vein, are the first ones stress damages. You carry more drugs, so exhaustion is a real hazard. And as leader, give a shaky partner a task, and speak up when a colleague is burning out.
slides.sayZh: 左栏是所有执照级别共有的：现场安全和 PPE、安全搬抬、叫支援、警察先行、开灯鸣笛要有理由，以及冷静、尊重的照护。右栏里，书里指出，作为院前急救员，你往往是现场受训最多的人，所以队员会照着你的安全习惯做。你要处理开静脉留下的锐器，所以必须会处理暴露。你最精细的操作，比如找静脉，最先被压力破坏。你要给的药更多，所以疲劳是真实的危险。作为领导，给发抖的搭档一个任务，同事出现倦怠时要开口。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Awake 18–20 hours: no driving, no drug administration
  • Stress steals fine motor control: breathe before the IV
  • Exposure: wash, report, evaluation, boosters, document
  • New gloves after the IV start; gloves off to drive
  • Anything entering the body must be sterilized
  • "Minor" calls can hide big problems: avoid tunnel vision
slides.say: Here are the risks that grow at PCP level. One, fatigue: after eighteen to twenty hours awake, don't drive or give medications. Two, stress steals fine motor control, so take a slow breath before you go for the vein or draw up the dose. Three, after a needlestick or splash: wash with soap and water right away, report it, get a medical evaluation and any boosters, and document. Four, fresh gloves after the IV start, and gloves off to drive. Five, anything that enters the body must be sterilized, not just disinfected. And six, don't brush off minor-sounding calls; tunnel vision causes missed findings.
slides.sayZh: 下面是在 PCP 层级变大的风险。一，疲劳：连续清醒十八到二十小时后，不开车、不给药。二，压力会偷走精细动作，所以找静脉、抽药之前先慢慢吸一口气。三，被针扎或被溅到后：立即用肥皂和水清洗、上报、接受医学评估和需要的加强针，并做好记录。四，开完静脉换新手套，开车前摘手套。五，任何进入身体的器械都必须灭菌，而不只是消毒。六，不要轻视听起来是「小事」的呼叫：隧道视野会让你漏掉重要发现。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Look after yourself: fuel, fitness, sleep; watch for burnout
  2. Grief: denial → anger → bargaining → depression → acceptance
  3. PCP safety: sharps, glove changes, exposure steps, rest before drugs

Next: Chapter 3, illness and injury prevention
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: look after yourself with good food, exercise, and enough sleep, and watch yourself and your partner for burnout. Two: grief often moves through denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance. After a hard call, a defusing comes right away; a formal debriefing comes twenty-four to seventy-two hours later. Three: PCP safety. Respect sharps, change gloves after the IV, know the exposure steps, and don't drive or give drugs when you're exhausted. Next lesson, Chapter 3, we look outward, at how paramedics prevent injuries before the call ever comes. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，照顾好自己：吃好、运动、睡够，并留意自己和搭档的倦怠信号。二，悲伤常经历否认、愤怒、讨价还价、抑郁、接受。艰难任务后，缓解会马上进行，正式汇报在二十四到七十二小时后。三，PCP 的安全：尊重锐器、开完静脉换手套、记住暴露处理步骤，太累时不开车也不给药。下节课，第三章，我们把目光转向外部：院前急救员怎样在呼叫到来之前就预防伤害。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
